releases.name: v0.1.5 — fix: exact compose matching, verified panels
v0.1.4 — docs: acme fixtures in the workspace example
releases.body:
**Docs — the workspace example now uses the demo's `acme` fixtures.** The `rundev.workspace.json` sample in
the README (`acme-api`, `acme-web`, `acme-app`) and the `cwd` JSDoc in `src/manifest.ts` now match the
throwaway workspace behind the screenshots and `docs/demo.tape`, so the docs and the demo tell the same
story. No functional changes.

**Upgrade**

```sh
opencode service restart   # re-resolves opencode-rundev@latest
```

releases.name: v0.1.3 — one panel per app
releases.body:
**Fix — a workspace `up` opened two panels.** The TUI picker dispatched every rundev command twice:
`session.command` resolves to `void`, so the guard `res !== undefined` never returned and the CLI
fallback always fired as well. One picker confirmation ran the verb twice — two `flutter run` splits
typed into the focused terminal, 3s apart (the server event log shows two `up: app` runs from a single
`select` event). The guard now checks that the client *exposes* the method, and the CLI path stays as
the fallback for an unreachable server.

**Fix — `interactive` services were never idempotent.** `statusOf` promised to report a panel as
running when a record existed, but nothing ever wrote one (the pidfile is only written for `process`),
so every `up` reported `unknown` and relaunched the panel. rundev now records the panel it opens and
`down` forgets it:

- a second `up` reports `already` instead of opening a duplicate panel;
- `up <svc> --force` relaunches on purpose (also exposed as a `force` in the agent tool), and an
  explicit `app@ios` over an android panel retargets instead of answering `already`;
- `check` — or `targets.<t>.check`, for a service that switches device — makes a panel verifiable:
  a closed app is detected and `up` relaunches by itself;
- the marker lives in its own file (`<name>.panel.json`): `stopProcess` kills by pidfile, and `pid: 0`
  would have addressed the whole process group. A defensive pid guard covers that path too;
- `logs` for an interactive service no longer claims "no log yet": the panel owns its output.

12 new smoke assertions cover the marker, `--force`, the retarget, the `.env` guard and the per-target
check. Prefer a verifiable setup when you write a manifest:

```jsonc
"app": {
  "kind": "interactive",
  "targets": {
    "android": { "device": "emulator", "envSection": "ANDROID", "requires": ["emulator"],
                 "check": "adb shell pidof com.example.app" }
  }
}
```

**Upgrade**

```sh
opencode service restart   # re-resolves opencode-rundev@latest
```

releases.name: v0.1.2 — one /rundev command
releases.body:
**Fix** — `/rundev` was registered twice: by the server plugin (`ctx.command.transform`) and by the TUI
plugin as a client slash command (`palette` + `slash`). OpenCode lists server commands and client slash
commands in the same completion surface with no dedupe, so the palette showed two identical `/rundev`
rows with nothing to tell them apart.

There is now a single command surface. The TUI no longer registers a command: at a workspace root the
server command emits a `select` event (`verb`, `workspace`, `members`, `sessionID`) and the TUI opens
the existing checkbox picker from it, then re-dispatches the chosen members to the server command.
Clients without a TUI still get the text menu as fallback.

**Upgrade**

```sh
opencode service restart   # re-resolves opencode-rundev@latest
```

releases.name: v0.1.1 — fix: TUI entrypoint deps
releases.body:
**Fix** — the TUI entrypoint (`src/tui.tsx`) needs `@opentui/solid` (JSX runtime) and `solid-js`, which were
declared as *optional* peer dependencies. Optional peers are not installed by npm, so loading the plugin
from the npm cache failed with:

```
Cannot find package '@opentui/solid' imported from .../opencode-rundev/src/tui.tsx
```

They are now regular `dependencies` (plus `@opentui/core`), verified by installing the published tarball
into a clean prefix and resolving them from the plugin file itself.

**Upgrade**

```sh
opencode service restart   # re-resolves opencode-rundev@latest
```
